metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Jersey Shore, PA
metaDescription: Jersey Shore sits in Lycoming County's dry-gas Marcellus core. Learn how dry-gas economics differ from wet gas and what your minerals may be worth.
heroLead: Jersey Shore sits along the West Branch of the Susquehanna in Lycoming County, right inside the dry-gas core of the Marcellus.
intro: People hear the name Jersey Shore, PA and assume it's a joke — it isn't, it's a real river town, and it happens to sit in one of the most heavily drilled dry-gas counties in the entire Marcellus play. Unlike the wet-gas acreage down in Westmoreland or Washington County, the gas coming up here is almost pure methane, and that changes how it's valued, marketed, and paid out.

sections.heading: Dry Gas Means a Simpler, More Volume-Driven Payout
paragraphs: Without natural gas liquids to separate and sell, dry-gas royalty around Jersey Shore is a function of volume produced and the Henry Hub or regional pricing point, minus whatever post-production costs your lease allows the operator to deduct. That's a simpler calculation than wet-gas country, but it also means your royalty tracks natural gas prices directly, with no NGL cushion when prices dip.

sections.heading: Lycoming's Long Drilling History
paragraphs: Operators have run horizontal Marcellus wells through Lycoming County for well over a decade now, and Jersey Shore-area units have generally seen consistent activity because the rock here is thick and the wells produce for a long time before declining. That track record gives us real royalty history to look at instead of speculation when we evaluate a parcel.

sections.heading: Fractional and Heir-Owned Interests Are Common Here
paragraphs: A lot of the farmland around Jersey Shore has been in the same families for generations, and it's common to find a mineral interest split six or eight ways among cousins who don't all agree on what to do with it. We're used to working through that kind of ownership, coordinating with everyone who holds a piece rather than requiring one person to make the decision alone.

faqs.question: Why does dry gas pay differently than wet gas?
faqs.answer: Dry gas royalty is based on gas volume and price alone, with no separate liquids revenue, so it moves more directly with natural gas prices than wet-gas acreage does.

faqs.question: My cousins and I all inherited a piece of the same tract — can you still buy it?
faqs.answer: Yes, we regularly work with multiple heirs on a single Jersey Shore-area interest, and we can structure an offer for individual shares or the whole group.

faqs.question: Has drilling around Jersey Shore slowed down?
faqs.answer: Activity has ebbed and flowed with gas prices over the years, but Lycoming County has stayed one of the more consistently drilled dry-gas counties in the state.
